title: Maximum Value of an Alternating Sequence
summary: Given integers n, s, and m, find the largest possible value in a valid alternating sequence of length n starting with s, where the absolute difference between consecutive elements does not exceed m.
statement: Given integers n, s, and m, find the largest possible value in a valid alternating sequence of length n starting with s, where the absolute difference between consecutive elements does not exceed m.
constraints: A valid length-n integer sequence starts at s and alternates strictly up/down or down/up.
Every adjacent absolute difference is at most m.
Return the largest value that can appear in any valid sequence.
hints: To grow successive peaks, alternate a rise of m with the smallest strict fall of one.
Each two steps can increase the peak by m-1.
Count complete two-step gains and handle the first rise.
The construction meets every bound and no alternating pair can gain more.
editorial: The construction meets every bound and no alternating pair can gain more.

tests.explanation: The sequence 3, 8, 7, 12 is valid and reaches the maximum twelve.
A single rise of three reaches seven.
